wizard.title: Set up in three steps
wizard.subtitle: You can skip it and come back later: “Settings” → “Setup wizard”.
wizard.cableOk: VB-CABLE found — Zoom, Meet and Discord will see the cleaned sound.
wizard.cableMissing: Without it other apps will not see the cleaned sound.
wizard.profileHint: Read any text for 15 seconds in silence — the model will remember the timbre.
confirm.resetText: Everything returns to factory values: devices, profile, level and sound processing. A/B takes and voice profiles stay on disk.
confirm.takeText: The current processing parameters will be replaced with those of take {stamp}. Devices and profile switch too.
sound.cableText: Zoom, Meet and Discord will not see the cleaned sound without VB-CABLE. One button, administrator rights once.
sound.channelHint: For a stereo interface. Summing channels with a phase difference comb-filters the voice — pick the one that carries it.
sound.cableAsMic: The virtual cable is selected as the microphone: the app will hear its own output and the sound of other programs. Choose a real microphone.
sound.outputVolumeHint: after all processing, the denoiser leaves it alone
sound.profileWeak: The profile is weak: the model will recognise the voice worse. Record a new one — 15 seconds in silence.
sound.profileOtherMic: The profile was recorded on another microphone ({device}); the model may not recognise your voice. Record a new one on this microphone.
sound.abHint: Raw and processed at the same position: switch on the fly, listen in headphones.
sound.abNeedCable: The take goes through processing: connect the virtual cable or turn on the headphone check.
sound.matchLevel: Match the level of the original
sound.applyTakeSettingsHint: restore the parameters this take was recorded with
settings.languageHint: The interface language. It follows Windows on the first launch and can be changed here afterwards.
settings.themeHint: Follow Windows, or pin the dark or light look.
settings.voice.onlyMineHint: VoxLock lets only your voice through. Off — the plain denoiser stays: easier on the CPU and no profile needed.
settings.voice.strengthHint: How much of the model's cleaned signal reaches the output. 1.00 is the strongest isolation; below that it sounds more natural but the background is louder.
settings.voice.maxSuppressionHint: Protection against dropouts: while you speak, the model output never falls further below the input than this. It applies only to your phrases — it does not bring music or the TV back in pauses. 0 — no protection: maximum isolation, but the model can occasionally swallow a word.
settings.voice.modeHint: “By profile” matches the recorded timbre — the most accurate. “Auto” works without a profile but lets other voices through more often.
settings.voice.toneHint: Two shelves after the auto level: body at 200 Hz and presence at 3 kHz. 0 dB leaves the sound unchanged.
settings.voice.bodyHint: A shelf at 200 Hz. Down removes boom and leftover hum, up adds density. Above +3 dB it brings back what the low cut takes away.
settings.voice.presenceHint: A shelf at 3 kHz where the consonants live. Up makes speech clearer but lifts the residual hiss too, hence the ±6 dB limit. There is nothing above 8 kHz: the model runs at 16 kHz.
settings.voice.deessHint: Ducks only the 5 kHz band and above when “s” and “sh” jump forward, so presence and air can be raised without hiss.
settings.voice.deessAmountHint: How far the sibilance can be pulled down. 6 dB suits most voices; more if the recording lisps.
settings.clean.levelingHint: Raises a quiet microphone to −26 dBFS before the model. Affects intelligibility and how even the level is.
settings.clean.residualHint: The more aggressive the stage, the harder it pushes the background and other voices down — and the higher the load and the risk of eating quiet syllables. GTCRN is the balance, DPDFNet and UL-UNAS are stronger.
settings.clean.residualMixHint: How much of the residual denoiser reaches the output. 100 % is the shipped behaviour; lower keeps quiet syllables but leaves more background.
settings.clean.vadHint: Closes the output in pauses by the speech detector, not by level. The background between words disappears and quiet words are not cut.
settings.clean.highPassHint: A 4th-order filter removes hum, wind and low-frequency knocking on the desk.
settings.clean.cutoffHint: The signal is attenuated below this frequency. 80–120 Hz removes hum; above that the voice itself starts to thin out.
settings.clean.airHint: Adds the top above 8 kHz that a 16 kHz model does not have: the voice stops sounding “muffled”. This is not a denoiser and not isolation — the 0–8 kHz band, the level and other voices stay the same. 0% is off.
settings.clean.gateHint: A threshold noise gate for what is left: it closes everything below the threshold.
settings.clean.gateThresholdHint: The level where the gate closes. Higher gives cleaner pauses but can cut quiet words; lower is gentler.
settings.clean.gateRatioHint: How hard the gate silences below the threshold: 1 is gentle, 10 is almost silence.
settings.clean.attackHint: How fast the gate opens. More is smoother, but the start of a word may be muted.
settings.clean.releaseHint: How fast the gate closes. More keeps word endings intact but holds the background longer.
settings.clean.holdHint: How long the gate stays open after the level drops, so word endings are not chopped off.
settings.clean.agcHint: Evenses out phrase levels: lifts quiet and lowers loud ones, but slowly, so the level does not jump inside a word. Works on your speech only.
settings.clean.agcTargetHint: The level the AGC pulls speech to. Lower is quieter and safer, higher is louder but closer to clipping.
settings.clean.agcMaxHint: The AGC's boost ceiling. A large one lifts the leftover noise too; 12–18 dB is enough for a quiet microphone.
settings.clean.limiterHint: Keeps the signal below 0 dB and clips peaks. Better left on.
settings.clean.comfortHint: A quiet steady background in pauses instead of “ringing” silence. Off by default.
settings.clean.comfortLevelHint: The comfort noise volume: −60…−70 dB is almost inaudible.
settings.clean.outputVolumeHint: Overall gain after all processing. Changes the volume only, the denoiser is left alone.
settings.latency.bufferAutoHint: Picks the smallest buffer without gaps: +20 ms on a miss, −10 ms after 90 s without misses. The value is remembered between launches.
settings.latency.bufferAutoHintShort: The current value was picked automatically. Turn auto off to set it by hand.
settings.latency.bufferHint: Headroom in the output ring. More is steadier and gap-free, but adds latency.
settings.latency.blockHint: The VoxLock block size: smaller is lower latency and higher load. 60 ms is the balance.
settings.latency.threadsHint: How many cores VoxLock gets. Up to 4 threads the processing time almost halves, beyond that it barely helps. “Automatic” picks the count from the machine and the block size.
settings.latency.why: Up to four threads the processing time almost halves; above that it barely helps but takes cores away from a game.
settings.latency.slow: With a {block} ms block and {threads} threads the model cannot keep up in real time — the sound will break up. Use 60 ms or more threads.
settings.control.muteHint: The global shortcut works from any program. “Hold” keeps the microphone on while the key is pressed (push-to-talk). Escape cancels the capture.
settings.diag.underrunsHint: Samples that did not reach the output; the brackets show the approximate duration. Growing means processing cannot keep up.
settings.diag.overflowsHint: Blocks that did not fit into the output ring and were lost. Zero is normal.
settings.diag.captureDropsHint: Microphone samples lost to an overflowing input ring. Zero is normal.
settings.diag.clockHint: Adaptation to the drift between the microphone and output clocks. 0 ppm means the converter runs exactly and neither tempo nor timbre changes.
settings.diag.logHint: The log lives in data/app.log: engine start and stop, device errors, model resets.
settings.app.autostartHint: Launch at sign-in: the app starts minimized to the tray.
settings.app.trayHint: The close button hides the window in the tray and processing keeps running.
settings.app.minimizedHint: The window is not shown at start: the app lives in the tray and processes sound right away.
settings.app.autoStartHint: As soon as the virtual cable is available, processing starts without pressing the button.
settings.app.followMicHint: If another default microphone is chosen in Windows, the app switches to it.
settings.app.keepAbHint: How many recent pairs to keep in data/recordings; older ones are deleted.
settings.app.licensesHint: The program is MIT-licensed. Third-party license texts ship next to it: the VoxLock, GTCRN and Silero models and the sherpa-onnx and ONNX Runtime libraries.
settings.app.exportHint: Export writes the settings file wherever you choose; import reads it back and restarts processing if it is running.
cable.installer: The installer has started. Press “Install Driver” and allow the installation.
cable.ready: Done: the virtual microphone is available.
cable.timeout: The installation did not finish. Close the installer and run it again; if the driver is already in place, restart the computer.
